claims.text: Udon and soba are prepared on-site and the kitchen handles wheat-based dishes throughout, so cross-contact with gluten is likely; no gluten-free protocol is documented.
The anago donburi is finished with a soy-sauce-based house sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
The signature udon/soba broth is made with Seto Inland Sea dried sardines (niboshi), so noodle dishes are not vegetarian or vegan; the menu centers on conger eel and oysters.
Fried chicken, karaage and breaded cutlets are cooked in shared oil with wheat-coated items, so gluten cross-contamination in the fryer is expected.
Set meals are seasoned in the standard Japanese teishoku style with wheat-based soy sauce and sauces.
Menu is dominated by chicken, meat and fish dishes with egg and animal dashi; no plant-based separation is documented.

name: 寿屋珈琲 幟町店 (Kotobukiya Coffee Noboricho)

claims.text: Black hand-dripped coffee is available from about 30 bean varieties, which is naturally plant-based for those avoiding dairy in their drink.
Plain black, flavored, and herbal teas are served by the pot and are naturally free of gluten and animal products, making a tea-only visit straightforward.
Lunch options are described as vegetable-forward, which may give more flexibility for plant-based diners who ask about ingredients.

name: 間借麺業 あらや識 (Magari Mengyo Araya Shiki)

claims.text: Wheat ramen/tsukemen noodles and wheat-containing soy-sauce broth are the core of every dish, so gluten is present throughout the kitchen.
The broth is a soy-sauce (shoyu) base, which in standard Japanese ramen contains wheat.
Broth is made from chicken and multiple dried fish (niboshi), and the shop is a daytime tenant inside a charcoal-grill (meat/fish) izakaya, so animal ingredients are pervasive.
Wheat noodles and wheat-based soy sauce are central to the menu, so gluten is present throughout the kitchen; no gluten-free handling is documented.
The dipping broth and tare for tsukemen rely on standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat.
Broths are made from fish stock and pork bone, and fish powder is used in dishes, so animal products are pervasive.
Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki is finished with a standard okonomi/Worcester-type sauce that is wheat- and soy-based.

name: Miyajima Guest House Mikuniya (宮島ゲストハウス三國屋)

claims.text: Gluten-free is accommodated only on advance request rather than by default; the standard dinner curry may use wheat-based roux/thickener, so confirm a wheat-free preparation when booking.
Self-service breakfast includes bread and cereal, presenting shared-surface gluten exposure at the morning buffet.
Japanese curry seasoning and soy sauce usually contain wheat; ask that the vegan curry be made with wheat-free/tamari seasoning for a gluten-free order.
The dinner curry is stated to contain no animal-derived ingredients at all (動物性食材は一切使用しておりません).
The house explicitly invites guests needing gluten-free to notify them in advance so they can accommodate it.
One of very few gluten-free-accommodating and fully vegan dinner options actually on Miyajima island, where evening dining is scarce.
